channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Council on Interaction with Maslikhats to be Established under the Kurultai
item.description: A Council on Interaction with Maslikhats will be established under the Kurultai, following a resolution passed by the assembly. The initiative aims to implement the President's directive for direct communication between regions and central state bodies. The Council will ensure Maslikhats' consistent participation in lawmaking and gather feedback on law implementation.

item.title: British Company Seeks New Copper Deposits in Kazakhstan
item.description: Central Asia Metals, a British company extracting copper from waste rock at the Konrat deposit, is exploring for new reserves in Kazakhstan. The company is conducting exploration at several promising sites. While copper production decreased slightly in Q3, overall production for the first nine months increased, meeting annual targets.

item.title: Almaty Metro's Kalkaman Station Nears 99% Completion, Set to Open by End of 2026
item.description: Construction of Almaty's Kalkaman metro station is 99% complete, with final assembly and commissioning underway. The station is expected to open by the end of 2026, improving public transport access. Three additional metro stations are planned towards the Baryk market, with over 45 billion tenge allocated.

item.title: Kazakhstan Opens Nuclear Emergency Center with U.S. Support Amidst Nuclear Power Expansion
item.description: Kazakhstan has launched a nuclear emergency center, supported by the U.S. Department of Energy, to monitor radiation and coordinate responses. This initiative comes as Kazakhstan, the world's largest uranium producer, plans to build nuclear power plants, following a referendum supporting nuclear energy.

item.title: Kazakhstan Deputy Raises Concerns Over Youth Involvement in Synthetic Drug Trafficking and Dropping
item.description: A member of the 'Adilet' party faction has raised concerns about youth involvement in synthetic drug trafficking and 'dropping' schemes. He highlighted statistics showing a significant number of minors convicted for drug offenses, urging for strengthened preventive measures.

item.title: Nukus Developing as a New Hub for Tourism and Investment with Major Infrastructure Projects
item.description: Nukus is being developed as a new center for tourism and investment, with significant infrastructure projects underway. A $78 million complex, including a 22-story five-star hotel and a 1,000-seat Congress-hall, is under construction to accommodate large tourist groups and events.

item.title: Kazakhstan Buys Nearly 36 Tons of Gold This Year, Ranking Among Leaders
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Bank has acquired nearly 36 tons of gold since the beginning of the year, placing it among major global buyers. Central banks worldwide have significantly increased gold purchases. In August alone, regulators bought 39 tons, a 69.6% increase from July and double the amount from August last year.

item.title: Ebola Cases in Congo Exceed 8,600, Health Institute Reports
item.description: The number of confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo has reached 8,665, with 4,178 deaths, according to the country's Public Health Institute. The mortality rate stands at 48.2%. Anti-epidemic measures are ongoing in affected provinces, with 890 patients hospitalized and 2,259 recovered. Vaccination efforts are showing positive results in some areas.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes Ethical AI Code and Climate Change Initiatives at Religious Leaders' Congress
item.description: Kazakhstan hosted the XXIV Secretariat meeting of the Congress of Leaders of World and Traditional Religions in Astana. Key outcomes include the adoption of documents on the role of religions in combating climate change and an ethical code for AI use in religion. The 'Charter of Rights for Terminally Ill Children' was also presented and supported.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Restore Degraded Land in Syr Darya Basin Amid Environmental Concerns
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans a four-year project to restore 264 hectares of degraded land in the Jalal-Abad region's Syr Darya basin. The initiative, supported by the UN's Food and Agriculture Organization and the Global Environment Facility, aims to improve forests and agricultural areas, benefiting over 27,000 people. It also seeks to sequester significant amounts of carbon dioxide.

item.title: Spiritual Diplomacy Aids Communication and Trust Restoration Amid Crises, Says Yerlan Karin
item.description: Spiritual diplomacy helps maintain communication channels and restore trust during crises, stated Yerlan Karin, Vice President of Kazakhstan and head of the Secretariat of the Congress of Leaders of World and Traditional Religions. He emphasized that Kazakhstan's constitutional values support its balanced foreign policy and that the congress serves as a unique platform for interreligious dialogue and project implementation.

item.title: Inflation Slowdown Eases Pressure on Kazakh Citizens' Incomes
item.description: Kazakhstan's annual inflation slowed to 9.3% in September 2026, down 0.5 percentage points from August, according to the Ministry of National Economy. Monthly price growth was 0.6%, with food prices decreasing for the second consecutive month. This slowdown is expected to reduce pressure on household incomes, which grew by 0.7% in the second quarter.

item.title: Uzbekistan Seeks Investment for Pharmaceutical Sector Development at Milan Exhibition
item.description: Uzbekistan is expanding opportunities for investment, production localization, and technology adoption in its pharmaceutical sector. International cooperation is key to this development. Meetings at the CPHI Milan 2026 exhibition aim to foster new collaborations, with a national "Made in Uzbekistan" stand showcasing local companies and projects.

item.title: CIS Foreign Ministers Discuss Summit Preparations, Security, and Economic Cooperation
item.description: Foreign ministers from CIS countries met in Ashgabat to discuss international agenda items and multilateral cooperation. Key topics included preparations for the upcoming CIS summit in Turkmenistan and the approval of statements on the CIS's 35th anniversary and preserving historical memory. Agreements were reached on strengthening cooperation in security, economy, and humanitarian spheres.

item.title: Almaty residents to receive heating support and contact information for issues
item.description: Almaty will operate a 24-hour "Rapid Response Headquarters" for the 2026-2027 heating season. Residents facing heating outages or issues can contact the 109 hotline, the Unified Dispatch Center at 225-14-31, or building management. Socially significant facilities will receive heat first, followed by residential buildings.

item.title: Kazakh banks' liquidity assessed amid potential mass deposit withdrawals
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Bank assessed banks' ability to withstand a sharp outflow of individual and corporate deposits. Even under a stress scenario with 60% withdrawals, some banks maintain significant liquidity reserves. The assessment used the Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) standard, with over half of banks failing the LCR in an extreme scenario.

item.title: Kazakhstan citizens' debt to banks reaches 26.5 trillion tenge
item.description: The total debt of Kazakhstan citizens to banks has increased to 26.5 trillion tenge. This figure reflects the growing financial obligations of individuals towards financial institutions within the country.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Russia Agree on 17 Joint Projects Worth $350 Million
item.description: Uzbekistan and Russia have agreed on 17 joint projects totaling $350 million in sectors like chemical industry, agriculture, and metallurgy, planned for launch in 2026. Bilateral trade increased by 10% in the first eight months of 2026, aiming for a total of $30 billion. Discussions also covered energy cooperation, including a nuclear power plant.

item.title: Tajikistan's Education Minister Defends Teachers Amidst Nurobod Assault Case
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Education stated he will defend teachers but cannot condone illegal actions, addressing a controversial case in Nurobod where a young teacher was reportedly assaulted and subsequently punished. The minister's remarks came amid public debate surrounding the incident and the teacher's fate.

item.title: Sultanate of Oman Becomes Eighth Shareholder of Eurasian Development Bank
item.description: The Sultanate of Oman will become the eighth shareholder of the Eurasian Development Bank (EDB). An agreement was signed during the Omani Sultan's visit to Kazakhstan. Oman is the first Gulf state to join the EDB, aiming to strengthen economic ties between Central Asia and the Gulf region.

item.title: New Uzbekistan City Development Includes Over 100 Projects, Smart Technologies
item.description: The development of New Uzbekistan in Tashkent involves over 100 projects, with construction reaching 3 million square meters by the end of 2025. The city is designed for 600,000 residents initially, with plans for 2 million, incorporating smart solutions and water-saving technologies. Educational and cultural facilities, including university campuses and a new library, are under construction.

item.title: US President Trump Expresses Interest in Visiting Uzbekistan
item.description: Donald Trump has shown interest in visiting Uzbekistan, according to a special envoy. This raises the possibility of the first visit by a sitting US president to Central Asia. Trump previously indicated a potential visit to Kazakhstan. US engagement with the region is increasing, with a summit and invitations from Central Asian leaders.

item.title: US Embassy Issues Warning Amid Suspected Plague Cases in Irkutsk
item.description: The US Embassy in Moscow issued a warning regarding suspected plague cases in Russia's Irkutsk region. The embassy noted that plague suspicion has not been officially confirmed. US citizens in the Irkutsk region are advised to follow local health requirements and avoid medical facilities related to the situation. Assistance from US authorities may be limited outside Moscow.

item.title: CAMCA Regional Forum Concludes, Focus Shifts to Advancing Cooperation
item.description: The 2026 CAMCA Regional Forum in Baku has concluded, with Uzbekistan set to host the 2027 event. The focus now shifts to leveraging the momentum and connections built to advance regional cooperation. The CAMCA Network, comprising over 300 leaders, will utilize platforms like CAMCA Talking magazine, TV, and podcasts to foster awareness and drive tangible collaboration across sectors.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Former president's son Atambaev faces 7.5-year prison sentence request
item.description: Prosecutors in Kyrgyzstan have requested a 7.5-year prison sentence for the son of former president Almazbek Atambayev. The specific charges and details of the case were not immediately available, but the request marks a significant development in legal proceedings involving the family of the ex-president.

item.title: Auditors Uncover 174 Illegal Constructions Amidst Land Grabbing Scandal in Kostanay
item.description: Kazakhstan's Supreme Audit Chamber has identified 174 instances of illegal land seizure in Kostanay. Citizens have built structures on these lands without proper documentation, bypassing tax and land registration systems. Authorities are now tasked with developing a plan to address these violations, with police investigating 143 cases and land management departments handling 31 others.

item.title: Ethnic and Linguistic Bias Alleged in Hiring Practices at Afghan Organizations, Including Taliban Influence
item.description: Sources within Afghan domestic and international organizations report ethnic and linguistic bias in hiring, favoring Pashto speakers under the guise of facilitating work with the Taliban. This allegedly leads to discrimination against other language groups. Taliban members reportedly sit on hiring committees, prioritizing Pashtun candidates.

item.title: Syr Darya Basin Youth Forum Addresses Water Management and Environmental Protection
item.description: The 4th Regional Youth Forum of the Syr Darya River Basin, held in Guliston, focused on youth participation in integrated water resource management and environmental protection. Participants from Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Kyrgyzstan discussed sustainable development, climate change, and the role of youth in addressing ecological issues. A model of the river basin was constructed to illustrate interconnections.

item.title: Kazakhstani Parents Seek Government Help for Sons Recruited into Russian Army
item.description: Relatives of Kazakhstani citizens recruited into the Russian army after going to Russia for work appealed to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Astana. They were informed that a special commission would review their applications. Some 21 Kazakhstani citizens are reportedly fighting in Luhansk.

item.title: Disagreement Between Taliban and Pakistan Discussed in Russia
item.description: A meeting in Russia, intended to discuss Afghanistan-related issues, concluded without results. The gathering was aimed at addressing disagreements between the Taliban and Pakistan, but the 'Moscow Format' yielded no outcome.

item.title: Zelenskyy: Putin's Birthday Missile Strikes Damaged Ukrainian Homes
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Russian missile and drone attacks on Putin's birthday targeted Ukraine, causing one of the "nastiest" strikes recently. The attacks hit 12 Ukrainian regions with 70 missiles and drones, killing 19 people.

item.title: Afghan Foreign Minister meets Iranian representative to discuss expanding bilateral relations
item.description: Amir Khan Muttaqi, Afghanistan's Foreign Minister, met with Mohammad Reza Bahrami, a representative from Iran's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, on the sidelines of the Moscow Format meeting. They discussed strengthening bilateral ties, regional developments, and mutual cooperation between Afghanistan and Iran.

item.title: Taliban Foreign Minister Meets Chinese Special Envoy on Afghanistan's Regional Situation
item.description: Taliban Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi met with China’s special envoy Yue Xiaoyong on the sidelines of the Moscow Format meeting. They discussed bilateral relations, the regional situation, and cooperation expansion. China emphasized joint efforts for regional stability and Afghanistan's economic connectivity.

item.title: Russian Company Expresses Interest in Investing in Afghanistan's Agriculture and Fertilizer Production
item.description: A Russian company, TEXHOTEKC, has expressed readiness to invest in Afghanistan's agriculture sector and chemical fertilizer production. The company plans to initially import fertilizers from Russia, followed by constructing a production plant within Afghanistan, according to the Taliban's Ministry of Agriculture.

item.title: Wildberries to Construct Major Logistics Hub in Uzbekistan
item.description: Russian e-commerce giant Wildberries has signed an investment agreement with Uzbekistan's Ministry of Investment, Industry, and Trade to build a large logistics complex. The facility, spanning 67.3 hectares in the Tashkent region, is expected to create at least 7,500 jobs. Construction is slated to begin by the end of October, with project work currently underway.

item.title: Dushanbe to Host Session on Improving Investment Climate
item.description: A special session, "Dialogue between State and Private Sector," will be held in Dushanbe on October 14, 2026, as part of the "Tajikistan Forward" entrepreneurial forum. The event aims to facilitate direct dialogue between government bodies, entrepreneurs, and investors to discuss challenges and propose solutions for improving the investment climate in Tajikistan.

item.title: Kabul Hosts Major Trade Expo Featuring Afghan and International Companies
item.description: A significant trade exhibition has opened in Kabul, showcasing industrial and agricultural products from approximately 600 Afghan and international companies. The five-day event aims to promote domestic production, strengthen trade ties, and highlight Afghanistan's economic potential to regional and global markets.

item.title: Afghan Deputy PM Opens Fifth Imam Abu Hanifa International Exhibition in Kabul
item.description: Mullah Abdul Ghani Baradar Akhund inaugurated the Fifth Imam Abu Hanifa International Exhibition in Kabul, featuring hundreds of Afghan and foreign companies. The seven-day event showcases products across various sectors, aiming to highlight Afghanistan's economic potential, support domestic production, and expand trade relations with the region.

item.title: Turkey May Establish Military Base in Saudi Arabia Under 'Mecca Pact'
item.description: Turkey may establish a military base in Saudi Arabia as part of the 'Mecca Pact.' The kingdom is expected to receive military contingent and air defense systems. Pakistan has reportedly sent weapons via four aircraft. This development signals a deepening of defense cooperation between the nations.

item.title: 48.5 kg of Narcotics Seized at Uzbek Border Crossing from Afghanistan
item.description: Uzbekistan's State Security Service (SSS) reported the seizure of 48.5 kg of narcotics at the "Ayritom" border customs post. The drugs, identified as 39 kg of hashish and 9.5 kg of opium, were found hidden in a truck originating from Afghanistan. A criminal case has been initiated.
